record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: For equivariant map algebras M(X,a)^Γ, where X is an affine scheme with coordinate algebra A, a is an algebra, Γ acts on X and a by automorphisms, and M(X,a)^Γ is the Γ-fixed subalgebra of a ⊗ A, determine classification criteria and invariants for the isomorphism problem. In particular, extend the known loop-algebra and two-variable multiloop-algebra results to the full multiloop case and then to more general equivariant map algebras.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.
4.2.1. Isomorphism problem. Characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism is one of the fundamental problems in the theory of EMAs.
It is therefore natural, though likely difficult, to try to generalize the results of both papers [ABP] and [GP07] to the multiloop case and beyond that to more general EMAs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let X be an affine scheme over k with coordinate algebra A = k[X], and let a be a (Lie or associative) algebra over k. Let Γ be a finite group acting on X by scheme automorphisms (inducing an action on A) and on a by algebra automorphisms. Consider the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗_k A, and define the equivariant map algebra

   M(X, a)^Γ := (a ⊗_k A)^Γ,

the Γ-fixed subalgebra. An important special case is the (twisted) multiloop algebra, where X = (k^×)^n, a is a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra, and Γ = Z/m_1 × ⋯ × Z/m_n acts on X by roots of unity and on a by commuting finite-order automorphisms.

Problem: Provide a complete set of classification criteria and isomorphism invariants for equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Γ. Specifically:

(a) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on two triples (X, a, Γ) and (X', a', Γ') for the corresponding equivariant map algebras to be isomorphic as algebras.

(b) Extend the existing isomorphism classifications known for (twisted) loop algebras (n = 1) and for two-variable (twisted) multiloop algebras (n = 2) to the case of (twisted) multiloop algebras of arbitrary number of variables n.

(c) Generalize the resulting classification to arbitrary equivariant map algebras M(X, a)^Γ beyond the multiloop case.
artifact.status_search_result: The isomorphism problem for equivariant map algebras is identified as a fundamental open problem in the area. Classification results are known for (twisted) loop algebras and for two-variable (twisted) multiloop algebras, but extensions to general multiloop algebras and to arbitrary equivariant map algebras remain open. Recent works on EMAs (e.g., 2025 work on interpolating categories) continue to treat the isomorphism classification problem in this generality as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizing EMAs up to isomorphism is one of the fundamental problems in the theory of EMAs. It is therefore natural, though likely difficult, to try to generalize the results ... to the multiloop case and beyond that to more general EMAs.
status_evidence.claim: Isomorphism classification of EMAs beyond the loop and two-variable multiloop cases is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Towards interpolating categories for equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on equivariant map algebras continues to reference isomorphism/classification problems in this generality.
status_evidence.claim: The general isomorphism problem for EMAs is still treated as an active research direction.
